business_problem: AgrInfo needed a practical way to digitize pig-farm management tasks such as barn monitoring, animal counting, and disease screening because manual oversight was slow, costly, and difficult to scale across large livestock operations.
solution_summary: AgrInfo used Baidu's EasyDL customization and serving platform to turn everyday pig-farm operations into computer-vision workflows that ordinary field teams could use. The company trained three models in about a week: an electronic-fence detector that monitors barns and identifies people or pigs entering key areas, an AI counting model that estimates pig numbers from ceiling-mounted camera images, and a pig-disease recognition model that analyzes body images for common symptoms before escalating atypical cases to remote experts. These models were embedded into applications such as Remote-eye and Pig Disease Assistant so users could access them through cameras, mobile uploads, and mini-program workflows rather than data-science tooling. The broader value is that EasyDL let AgrInfo encode husbandry know-how into reusable AI services, connecting video frames, object detection, disease screening, and remote diagnostics in one agricultural management pipeline.
products_used: EasyDL Customized Training and Serving Platform

solution_components.name: Electronic Fence Model
solution_components.role: Detects people and pigs in monitored barn areas to support safety and activity observation.

solution_components.name: AI Counting Model
solution_components.role: Counts pigs from barn images so farms can monitor herd size remotely.

solution_components.name: Pig Disease Recognition Model
solution_components.role: Screens pig images for disease symptoms and flags cases that need expert review.

solution_components.name: Remote-eye

solution_components.name: Pig Disease Assistant
solution_components.role: Uses disease-recognition results to help breeders assess pig health and escalate uncertain cases.

data_flow: Barn-camera images and farmer-captured pig photos enter EasyDL-trained detection models, which classify presence, count animals, and screen for visible disease traits. The results are sent into Remote-eye and Pig Disease Assistant workflows, where users monitor farms remotely, review suspected health issues, and escalate non-typical cases to online experts.
business_outcome: AgrInfo reduced manual farm-inspection effort, improved herd visibility and disease screening, and showed that livestock know-how can be packaged into reusable AI services for day-to-day farm management.
metrics: Three models were trained within 1 week.
All three models achieved about 80% accuracy.
Counting and disease-recognition workflows reduced the need for weekly on-site inspections.
architecture_clues: The system links detection models to operational products such as Remote-eye and Pig Disease Assistant instead of leaving them as standalone experiments.
Ceiling-mounted cameras and mobile phone uploads are both part of the data-ingestion strategy.
Non-typical disease cases are escalated to remote experts rather than forced through full automation.
